_about: Practical, sourced information for families, collected by hand from each board's own pages and documents, and inherited by every school page of that board. Every record links to the official page it came from and carries the date it was checked. We summarise in plain words and never copy policy text at length. kind: rule = a published rule (applies to everyone it describes); process = how to ask, where the answer is decided case by case; decision = something the board has approved; proposal = a recommendation not yet decided; projection = a forecast in a published plan; not_found = we looked and the board does not publish it (say so rather than guess). applies: which school levels a record is for. lifecycle: dates (deadlines, registration windows) go stale fastest, rules and plans last longer. Never add a record you have not read on the board's own page. Start a new board by copying one board's block and checking every link. See docs/board-info.md.

records.title: Register for School
records.summary: Register online, with the board's fillable form, or at your home school. You need proof of your child's age and proof of a Niagara address; an up-to-date immunization record must be on file with the public health unit. Families whose children were born outside Canada start with the DSBN Welcome Centre.

records.title: School Locator
records.summary: The board's own lookup: enter an address to see its area school and the school's mapped boundary (choose the school year first). The board says its maps show general layout only; its planning department answers boundary questions.

records.title: French Immersion
records.summary: DSBN has one entry point: French Immersion starts in Grade 1, with no French needed beforehand. Families register during a yearly window; when we checked, the board had not yet posted the dates or information sessions for the next intake. Transportation follows the same rules as for every DSBN student.

records.title: Secondary programs
records.summary: French Immersion continues in Grades 9 to 12 at five DSBN high schools (listed on the board's French Immersion schools page). Core French is offered at every DSBN high school.

records.title: Attending a school outside your area
records.summary: We could not find a published DSBN procedure for asking to attend a school other than your area school. Ask the school's principal, or the board's planning department, how requests are handled and when to apply. Bus service to a school other than your home school is only provided for approved system-wide programs (see transportation).

records.title: Transportation Eligibility and Service (board policy)
records.summary: Students who live at least 0.8 km (kindergarten), 1.6 km (Grades 1 to 8) or 3.2 km (Grades 9 to 12) from their home school, by the shortest walking route, may get transportation. Students attending a school other than their home school get it only for approved system-wide programs. Niagara Student Transportation Services runs the buses for DSBN and Niagara Catholic.

related.title: Check transportation eligibility for an address (NSTS)

records.title: Special Education
records.summary: The board's special education page, with its special education report (the board's plan for programs and services) and a guide for parents. Start with your child's teacher and principal; they arrange assessments, Individual Education Plans (IEPs) and Identification, Placement and Review Committee (IPRC) meetings.

records.title: Special Education Advisory Committee (SEAC)
records.summary: SEAC meets monthly in public and advises the board on special education programs and services. Its members include representatives of local community associations.

records.title: Multi-Year Accessibility Plan 2023-2028 (PDF)
records.summary: The board's accessibility plan under Ontario's accessibility law. It describes board-wide plans, not the features of a particular school building; ask the school about specific needs.

records.title: DSBN Welcome Centre
records.summary: Registration, settlement and language support for families new to Canada. English as a Second Language support is described on the board's ESL page.

related.title: ESL: English as a Second Language

records.title: Long Term Accommodation Plan 2023-2032 (PDF)
records.summary: The board's plan for school space: each school's capacity, enrolment and projections, and recommended projects by planning area. Recommendations are not decisions. The plan notes that the province's 2017 moratorium on school closures stops accommodation reviews until it is lifted.

related.title: Accommodation Review policy (marked under review because of the 2017 moratorium)

records.title: Student Achievement Plan
records.summary: The board's plan under Ontario's student achievement framework: literacy (EQAO reading and writing, the OSSLT), graduation and credits, and engagement and well-being (suspensions). It reports board results next to Ontario's; it does not set numeric targets. These are board-wide figures, not this school's.

records.title: Parent Involvement Committee (PIC)
records.summary: A parent committee that advises the board. Meetings are public and listed on the page.

records.title: School councils
records.summary: Every school has a parent-led school council; ask the school how to join.

records.title: Board of Trustees
records.summary: Your elected trustees, by area, and how to reach them. Board and committee meetings are public.

records.title: Contact us
records.summary: Start with your child's teacher, then the principal; if that doesn't settle it, contact the school's superintendent. The board's complaints policy sets out the steps.

records.title: Welcome to Niagara Catholic (registration)
records.summary: Start online, then finish at the school in person with your child's birth certificate, a baptism record (the child's or a parent's), proof of address and any custody papers. Baptized Catholic children, and children with a Catholic parent, are entitled to attend a Catholic elementary school; the board also accepts other children at the principal's discretion. Students do not need to be Catholic to attend a Niagara Catholic high school.

records.title: Admission of Elementary and Secondary Students (procedure 301.1, PDF)
records.summary: Students attend the home school for their address. To ask for a school outside your area, meet the principal and submit the board's request form; the Family of Schools superintendent approves or refuses in writing. If approved, parents are responsible for transportation. The procedure gives no application deadline.

records.title: Which school do I attend? (Niagara Student Transportation Services)
records.summary: The board's own "finding your home school" link goes to this lookup, run by its transportation consortium. Choose Niagara Catholic and the school year. The transportation office has the final word if anything disagrees.

records.title: French Immersion
records.summary: French Immersion starts in Grade 1. Registration opens once a year in January (for 2026-27 it ran January 12 to 30); the board posts each year's dates on this page. Places go first to siblings of current Immersion students, then to children inside the school's boundary, then to others if space allows, with a waitlist kept until September 30.

records.title: French Immersion
records.summary: French Immersion continues in Grades 9 to 12 at four Niagara Catholic high schools. There is no separate online registration for secondary French Immersion.

records.title: Student Transportation Policy (500.2)
records.summary: Students who live at least 0.8 km (kindergarten), 1.6 km (Grades 1 to 8) or 3.2 km (Grades 9 to 12) from their home school, by the shortest walking route, may get transportation. Families of students approved to attend outside their area provide transportation themselves. Niagara Student Transportation Services runs the buses.

related.title: Check transportation eligibility for an address (NSTS)

records.title: Special Education
records.summary: The board's special education page, with its 2026-2027 Special Education Plan and a guide for parents and guardians. Start with your child's teacher and principal; parents give written consent before assessments.

records.title: Special Education Advisory Committee (SEAC)
records.summary: SEAC holds monthly public meetings during the school year at the Catholic Education Centre and advises the board on special education.

records.title: Accessibility
records.summary: The board's 2022-2027 Multi-Year Accessibility Plan, reviewed every two years. It describes board-wide plans, not the features of a particular school building; ask the school about specific needs.

records.title: Newcomer and English language support
records.summary: We could not find a Niagara Catholic page for newcomer families or English language learners. Ask the school what support is offered; registration asks for proof of immigration status.

records.title: 2024-2029 Long Term Accommodation Plan (PDF)
records.summary: The board's plan for school space: capacity, enrolment, projections and recommended reviews by family of schools. Its recommendations are subject to public consultation and are not decisions.

records.title: Student Achievement Plan (PDF)
records.summary: The board's plan under Ontario's student achievement framework: reading, writing and math (EQAO and the OSSLT), graduation, credits, pathways, suspensions, attendance and awareness of mental health supports, each next to Ontario's. It does not set numeric targets. These are board-wide figures, not this school's.

records.title: Niagara Catholic Parent Involvement Committee
records.summary: Meets every other month during the school year and links parents, Catholic School Councils, the Director of Education and trustees. Each school has a Catholic School Council; ask the school how to join.

records.title: Trustees
records.summary: Your elected trustees, by area, and how to reach them. Board meetings are public; dates, agendas and minutes are posted.

records.title: Student and Family Support Office
records.summary: Start with the teacher, then the principal, then the Family of Schools superintendent; if it is still not settled, the Student and Family Support Office helps. The office aims to acknowledge within 2 business days.

records.title: Long Term Accommodation Plan 2023-2032, Elementary Planning Area 13 (PDF)

facts.capacity_definition: On-the-ground (OTG) capacity: the provincially recognized pupil space of the building, not counting portables

records.summary: The board's 2023 plan lists this school as Grades 1 to 8 French Immersion with an on-the-ground capacity of 322 and 495 students in 2022, and says it is over capacity and expected to stay over capacity long term. It lists no upcoming project for this planning area. Projections are the board's forecasts, and capacity is building space, not open seats in a grade or program.

decisions.title: Saint Michael and Saint Paul family of schools attendance area review (Niagara Falls)
decisions.summary: On June 16, 2026 the board approved new attendance boundaries ("Option 2") for this family of schools. They take effect when the new South Niagara Falls Catholic elementary school opens; the board had not published an opening date when we checked. Check the review page for the new boundary for your address.
decisions.match: Names in the approved motion matched by hand to this site's schools in Niagara Falls (Our Lady of Mount Carmel, Sacred Heart, Loretto, Father Hennepin, St. John Henry Newman, St. Patrick, St. Mary, St. Gabriel Lalemant, St. Vincent de Paul, Mary Ward, Notre Dame, Saint Michael CHS, Saint Paul CHS).

school_programs._about: Programs a board lists on its own pages, by school. Matched by hand: board list name + city, checked against the school's grade range. Shown next to the Ministry's FSL list; when they disagree, the page shows both and says so.
